Why Is My Telegram Channel Posting Twice? (Duplicate Posts, Explained)
Double posts are annoying for subscribers and make a channel look automated in the worst way. The good news: the cause is nearly always one of four things.
1. Another account still schedules the channel
The most common cause after a migration or team handover: the old account's schedules were never removed. Both accounts happily queue posts for the same time. Fix: in the
other
account, open
and delete its schedules (or disconnect the channel). If you cannot access the old account, remove the bot from the channel's admin list — that stops the posting immediately.
2. Two sender bots are admin in the channel

Every channel must pair with exactly one sender bot, and that bot should be the only bot with posting rights. If you created a second bot and added it as admin, posts may arrive from both. Keep one sender bot per channel as admin; remove extra bots from the channel.
3. The message got scheduled twice
Easy to do when re-sending the same text after an edit, or when importing while old schedules exist. Open the Message List for the day and scan for same-time twins before the posting window. The
view makes clusters obvious.
4. The recurrence rule was duplicated, not edited
Creating a new daily rule instead of editing the existing one produces two identical posts every day. Check the recurring list — if two rules share the same text and time, delete one.

Common questions
Does Fast Scheduler retry a post that failed, causing doubles?
A retry only happens when the send did not confirm. If Telegram accepted the post but the confirmation was lost (rare network hiccup), you can get one duplicate. It does not re-send confirmed posts.
Can I merge two accounts scheduling the same channel?
Yes — export from the old account, import with Add on the new one, then clear the old account. Never leave both active.

Here is exactly what happens from click to Premium days, for both sides.
1. Click.
A new user opens your link and starts the bot. The click is recorded instantly, but nothing is granted yet — this is what the "pending" state in your list means.
2. Verify.
The new user connects a channel and schedules at least 1 message — the same verification you completed to unlock the program. Until then, the referral stays pending.
3. Credit.
The moment they qualify,
both of you receive 3 Premium days

under Available days). If you already have paid Premium, the days wait in your balance until it ends.
4. Activate.
On the free plan, activate earned days from the referral menu — a Premium period starts immediately. Used days move to the Used counter so you always see earned, used and available totals.
Limits.

website\\help\\a\\referral_verify.html: Why Verification Is Required — Fast Scheduler Help
To unlock the Referral Program you must
. This is not bureaucracy — it is how we verify your account is real.

Every referral reward is paid out as Premium time, and Premium time costs us real money (Telegram Stars fees and server costs). Without verification, anyone could spin up dozens of empty accounts in minutes and drain the reward pool — which would force us to shut the program down for everyone, including honest users.

Connecting a channel proves you have something real to post to; scheduling a message proves you actually use the bot. Both checks are automatic and take most users under two minutes: send your channel link in Step 1 of the tutorial, then schedule any post — even a test message to yourself counts.
What we check — and what we don't.

We only look at anonymous counters (channels connected, messages created). We never read your message contents, never ask for documents or phone numbers, and never share anything with third parties. Verification is purely about activity, not identity.
Opening the Referral menu before verifying shows a locked screen — that is expected, not a bug. Finish the two steps above and the menu unlocks by itself; nothing else is required.
